hypothesis: The quadrature reference (N_g = 401 on [-8,8]) is valid across every configuration the project uses, not only at the frozen point where it was validated: five innovation families x four correlations x twelve levels.
design: For each (family, rho, L, seed) the same 256 chains are scored on seven candidate grids and on a finer reference grid (3201 points on [-12,12]); three diagnostics per grid: the worst-chain posterior mass in the outermost 2% of the domain (truncation), max_j |sum_i K(g_i|g_j) w_i - 1| (quadrature error at source), and the relative RMS difference of the posterior-mean field against the reference grid on the same chains (what a reported number would move by). 4 seeds.
predeclared_analysis: tools/make_grid_numbers.py: the worst drift over all (family, rho, level) at the frozen grid, and the grid at which drift first falls below 1e-4; the table is the maximum over configurations, not the mean, because the claim is a bound.
